claim: SARS-CoV-2 presents an unprecedented international challenge.
source: SARS-CoV-2 presents an unprecedented international challenge, but it will not be the last such threat.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 will not be the last pandemic threat.
source: SARS-CoV-2 presents an unprecedented international challenge, but it will not be the last such threat.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future pandemic threats based on historical patterns.

claim: A Global Immunological Observatory should be at the heart of pandemic preparedness.
source: We propose that a Global Immunological Observatory and associated developments in systems immunology, therapeutics and vaccine design should be at the heart of this enterprise.
evidence: This is the main proposal of the manuscript, representing the authors' argument based on inference from current pandemic challenges.

claim: The time from release of the SARS-CoV-2 sequence to a needle in an arm in the first Phase one vaccine trial was only 65 days.
source: The time from release of the SARS-CoV-2 sequence to a needle in an arm in the first Phase one vaccine trial was only 65 days (https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT04283461).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a clinical trial registry.

claim: The rapid vaccine development was made possible through recently developed easily manufactured, implementable and deployable vaccine platforms, such as mRNA or DNA constructs.
source: This is a remarkable achievement made possible through the recent development of easily manufactured, implementable and deployable vaccine platforms, such as mRNA or DNA constructs.
evidence: This is an inference about the factors enabling rapid vaccine development, drawing on established knowledge about vaccine platform technologies.

claim: Permissive animal challenge models should be established to test vaccines.
source: Contemporaneously, permissive animal challenge models should be established to test the vaccine and also to aid in the identification of neutralizing monoclonal antibodies which could be used in short term prevention and as therapeutic agents.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on established scientific practice and inference about pandemic response needs.

claim: Animal challenge models can aid in the identification of neutralizing monoclonal antibodies which could be used in short term prevention and as therapeutic agents.
source: Contemporaneously, permissive animal challenge models should be established to test the vaccine and also to aid in the identification of neutralizing monoclonal antibodies which could be used in short term prevention and as therapeutic agents.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of how animal models are used in immunological research.

claim: Neutralizing monoclonal antibodies can be identified in people who have recovered from infection.
source: This endeavor should go hand in hand with identification of neutralizing monoclonal antibodies in people who have recovered from the infection as well as with detailed analysis of their T cell responses.
evidence: This is based on established immunological knowledge about antibody responses to infection.

claim: With 'peacetime' sampling of reservoir species by GIO and GPO, a library of mRNA/DNA vaccine candidates could be generated preemptively.
source: Indeed, with 'peacetime' sampling of reservoir species by GIO and GPO, a library of mRNA/DNA candidates could be generated preemptively.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about what could be achieved with the proposed GIO/GPO infrastructure.

claim: GIO could provide considerable insights into other immune-related diseases: from cancer to autoimmune disorders.
source: More broadly, GIO could provide considerable insights into other immune-related diseases: from cancer to autoimmune disorders.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about potential broader applications of the proposed GIO.

claim: A Global Immunological Observatory is essential for understanding and combating future pandemics.
source: We argue that a Global Immunological Observatory is essential for understanding and combating future pandemics.
evidence: This is the central argument of the manuscript, based on inference from current pandemic challenges.

claim: The GIO/GPO infrastructure would bootstrap our ability to engage with fundamental questions associated with key processes in pandemics, such as the transmission process.
source: The GIO/GPO infrastructure would bootstrap our ability to engage with a series of fundamental questions associated with the other key processes in pandemics, such as the transmission process – encompassing the biophysics of pathogen spread between individuals, as well as the role of patterns of social mixing.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the capabilities of the proposed infrastructure.

claim: To make full use of immunological and pathogen observatories, cross fertilization between many fields will be required: spanning systems immunology, virology and physical sciences, through to public health and social science.
source: To make full use of immunological and pathogen observatories, cross fertilization between many fields will be required: spanning systems immunology, virology and physical sciences, through to public health and social science.
evidence: This is an inference about the interdisciplinary requirements for the proposed observatory.

claim: Major progress in computational biology and disease modeling would be enabled by the rich and varied datasets from GIO/GPO.
source: Major progress in computational biology and disease modeling would also be enabled by these rich and varied datasets.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential impact of GIO/GPO data.

claim: A key gap in pandemic and endemic disease understanding is the cross-scale phylodynamic interaction between viral evolution and immune kinetics in individuals and nonlinear epidemic dynamics at population and global scales.
source: In particular, a key gap in pandemic and endemic disease understanding is the cross-scale phylodynamic interaction between viral evolution and immune kinetics in individuals and nonlinear epidemic dynamics at population and global scales (Grenfell et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Establishment of GIO/GPO would generate a step change in knowledge at the interface between viral evolution and immune kinetics.
source: Establishment of GIO/GPO would generate a step change in knowledge at this key interface.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the impact of the proposed infrastructure.

claim: GIO and a larger pathogen enterprise will require significant annual investments, but this will be trivial compared to the costs of future pandemics.
source: GIO and a larger pathogen enterprise will require significant annual investments, but this will be trivial compared to the costs of future pandemics.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of investment costs versus pandemic costs.

claim: Establishing GIO/GPO would require solving a range of important practical issues, from sustainable funding, governance, global equity, intellectual property and relationships with industry.
source: Establishing GIO/GPO would require solving a range of important practical issues, from sustainable funding, governance, global equity, intellectual property and relationships with industry, but there are existing models and clear paths to addressing all of these challenges (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an inference about practical implementation challenges, with reference to a figure.

claim: There are existing models and clear paths to addressing the practical challenges of establishing GIO/GPO.
source: Establishing GIO/GPO would require solving a range of important practical issues, from sustainable funding, governance, global equity, intellectual property and relationships with industry, but there are existing models and clear paths to addressing all of these challenges (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a claim based on inference from existing institutional models, with reference to a figure.

claim: Lessons for infrastructure, funding and governance could be learned from the virological and immune phenotypes collected to inform strain selection for seasonal influenza vaccination coordinated by the WHO.
source: Lessons for infrastructure, funding and governance could also be learned from the virological and immune phenotypes collected to inform strain selection for seasonal influenza vaccination coordinated by the WHO (Morris et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to work on influenza surveillance.

claim: The skill of weather forecasts was dramatically improved by deployment of buoys measuring Sea Surface Temperature across the oceans of the world.
source: The skill of weather forecasts was dramatically improved by deployment of buoys measuring Sea Surface Temperature across the oceans of the world (http://www.argo.ucsd.edu/About_Argo.html).
evidence: This is a claim supported by a citation to information about the Argo buoy system.

claim: Early warning and rapid response can make dramatic differences that translate directly to immensely favorable outcomes in pandemics.
source: And as this pandemic has repeatedly shown, early warning and rapid response can make dramatic differences that translate directly to immensely favorable outcomes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from observations of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.

claim: Susceptibility and immunity have been the 'dark matter' of epidemic dynamics.
source: Susceptibility and immunity have been the 'dark matter' of epidemic dynamics; GIO could reveal them, to the considerable benefit of global health.
evidence: This is a characterization based on established knowledge about gaps in epidemic modeling.

claim: GIO could reveal susceptibility and immunity patterns, to the considerable benefit of global health.
source: Susceptibility and immunity have been the 'dark matter' of epidemic dynamics; GIO could reveal them, to the considerable benefit of global health.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential impact of GIO.

claim: The necessary technologies for GIO/GPO fundamentally already exist.
source: The necessary technologies fundamentally already exist.
evidence: This is a claim based on knowledge of current technological capabilities.

claim: Assays to measure the breadth, affinity, receptor binding competition analyses and neutralizing capacity of specific antibodies would be a critical part of the pandemic response process.
source: Finally, and this all flows logically from the initial serological signal and identification of the pathogen's sequence and in vitro production of its proteins, the establishment of assays to measure the breadth, affinity, receptor binding competition analyses and neutralizing capacity of specific antibodies would be a critical part of this process.
evidence: This is based on established immunological knowledge and inference about pandemic response needs.

claim: All pandemic response activities (vaccine development, animal models, antibody identification, assay establishment) can and should be done in parallel.
source: Importantly, all these activities can and should be done in parallel.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on inference about optimal pandemic response strategies.

claim: An essential condition for GIO/GPO is the transparent and effective governance of administrative, informatics and laboratory cores.
source: A variety of distributed models are possible for GIO/GPO, but an essential condition is the transparent and effective governance of administrative, informatics and laboratory cores.
evidence: This is an inference about requirements for successful implementation of the proposed infrastructure.

claim: Understanding of spatio-temporal dynamics is crucial to addressing weather and climate science problems.
source: Another field where understanding of spatio-temporal dynamics is crucial to addressing a deeply applied problem is weather and climate science.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about weather and climate science.

claim: We have the means to deploy measurements crucial both to pandemic preparedness and endemic disease control, using the immune systems as sensors.
source: Similarly, in the context of global health, we have the means to deploy measurements crucial both to pandemic preparedness, and endemic disease control, using the delicate and responsive sensor that is all of our immune systems (and the immune systems of all the reservoir species).
evidence: This is an inference about the potential use of immune systems as surveillance tools.
